newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Sep wheat up on lack of deliveries, spreads.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Sep wheat up on lack of deliveries, spreads.

text.p: CBOT September wheat futures were up sharply on less-than-expected deliveries posted on Tuesday and on cash-connected bull spreading, traders said.
"There's been virtually nothing delivered and that's what is pushing the September up," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
There were 20,000 bushels of wheat posted for delivery on Tuesday. Traders had expected three million to five million bushels of wheat to be delivered in the first few days.
Traders said The Chicago Corporation was a noted September/December spreader while SAK Trading bought two million bushels December.
Also lending support were greater-than-expected export inspections to China in Tuesday's USDA export inspection report, traders said.
Wheat had opened weaker on ideas U.S. air strikes against Iraq on Tuesday would disrupt oil-for-food talks.
Funds reportedly were heavy sellers of wheat on the open but the market turned firm after FIMAT and Cargill both became buyers, traders said.
At 1033 CDT, wheat was 3-1/2 to seven cents per bushel higher with September up seven up $4.55-1/2 a bushel and December rose 3-3/4 to $4.57 in fast dealings.
